title: The Wreck (on the sea kit)
part: The sea kit on the thunderbolt, the wreck and Charybdis
hypothesis: The thunderbolt, the wreck and Charybdis read without narration if the sea is a working brick ocean, the bolt is seen to hit the mast held in the frame before it, the ship visibly breaks up and her men go into the water (not through her), and Charybdis is a whirlpool that turns and swallows the timbers.
variable: look.sea on every key (dusk calm, the fair wind, the storm and the aimed bolt, the wreck, the whirl, camera paths for the strike, the keel and Charybdis); K4 and K5 restaged (Odysseus astride the keel, the drowned crew left where they fell, Odysseus's hang under the fig's canopy, the old whirlpool prop out, a dawn look for K5); a SWIM for Odysseus added to the director's module and the sheet recompiled (the compiler's current output for all six figures). The shot plan re-solved on it.

metrics_after.clip: CLIP OD-B12-S07 visible 0.0 s in 0 intervals
metrics_after.note: a first render (85.6 min) was thrown away: the wreck's hiding of the hull leaked into the keys before the break (a later drawing visited while the cameras were solved left it hidden), so the ship was missing for 0-27 s; fixed in the kit and rendered again

checks.test: no one runs through anything: feet on the deck as she heaves; the thrown men in the water, not in the hull; Odysseus on the keel, not in it
checks.note: tools/metis/clip.js on the take: 0 visible intervals. Before the fixes the pre-render check found the crew thrown overboard through the hull's sides and standing in it as it rolled (37-41 s), two pairs of swimmers inside each other on their way to the K4 marks, and Odysseus seated 0.17 H into the keel. Now the hull is gone at the break (look.sea wreck, 36.9 s) and the men are let down into the water at their swimming times, the drowned sink 14 plates out of sight, the K4 crew drown where they fell, Odysseus swims (a SWIM added to the director's module) and sits astride the keel 17 units up

checks.test: the saving timber is visible before the strike; the bolt strikes the mast
checks.note: a wide on its own camera path (24.2-28.2 s) holds the whole hull and mast as the cloud comes; the bolt (look.sea bolts: trans-yellow plates from the cloud to the masthead, riding the hull) at 26.6 s with the cold flash; the masthead burns after

checks.test: Charybdis reads as a whirlpool that takes the timbers and gives them back
checks.note: seven stepped rings of tiles turning faster toward a dark eye, a white spiral laid across them; the keel carried round and drawn under (depth 3 to 8 plates at 49.5-50.8 s) and thrown back up (to 2 at 59 s) while he hangs from the fig

checks.test: the solved plan's shots are legal
checks.note: 5 of 7 legal; the two wides of the wreck (35.7-51.5 s) fail the solver's own test; 41.6-51.5 s is covered by the kit's own camera paths; one drawing at 28.3 s is filled by the baked sail

result: Published as take 2. The bolt hits the mast in a wide that holds the ship, she breaks up into timbers, her men drown in the water, Odysseus rides the keel, and Charybdis turns, swallows the keel and gives it back. Loose: two of the seven solved shots fail their legality (the wreck wides); one drawing at 28.3 s is filled by the baked sail; the mast does not visibly fall on the helmsman (the hull's mast is part of the hull piece); the break is a cut from whole hull to timbers on one drawing; the sheet was recompiled, so every figure's motion is the current engine's, not take 1's.
